item.title: 2027: APC, ADC at daggers drawn over attack on Tinubu’s convoy
item.description: ABUJA — The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council, APC-PCC, and African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, ADC-PCC, were yesterday locked in verbal war over last weekend’s attack on the convoy of President Bola Tinubu in Abuja. While the APC-PCC accused the opposition African Democratic Congress ADC and the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, of sponsoring the hoodlums who pelted the President’s motorcade with stones, ADC-PCC challenged the ruling party to produce evidence that the opposition party sponsored the attack. In a statement, the spokesperson of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Mr Dele Alake, said the opposition parties were arming young Nigerians and sending them to disrupt the party’s rallies. “To create the false narrative of citizens’ discontent against the President, the ADC and NDC now sponsor hoodlums, arm them with cudgels and banners, and commandeer them to chant ‘Bamaiyi’ at APC campaign rallies,” the statement said. It described the mosque incident as “the latest instance of this abhorrent and anti-democratic stunt,” adding that it amounted to “the desecration of an Abuja Mosque last Friday, where these thugs were mobilised to pelt the presidential motorcade with stones.” The council said it had seen it coming, adding that “hours before the flag-off of our presidential campaign rally in Kaduna on October 24, 2026, we alerted Nigerians to the plot by opposition elements to create undue tension, sow disharmony, and introduce violence into the campaigns across the country.’’ According to the statement, the opposition parties had perfected elaborate schemes to use deepfakes, artificial-intelligence-generated images, fake news, sponsored protests, and other forms of propaganda “to manipulate public opinion and spread lies about our nation, President Bola Tinubu, the All Progressives Congress, and the processes leading to next year’s general elections.” “These unpatriotic and disingenuous plots by opposition elements have started unfolding. Their major objective is to deceive Nigerians and the international community by driving a narrative of discontent against President Tinubu”, the council said. It praised the security personnel attached to the presidential convoy for their maturity and for exercising utmost restraint in such a delicate situation. “We also commend the fatherly disposition of President Tinubu, who has since directed the Police Command in Abuja to release those detained for the infraction,” the statement said. item.title: NDIC urges corps members to save in insured banks
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu AWKA — The Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC) has urged members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) in Anambra State to cultivate sound financial habits and ensure they save their money in banks insured by the corporation. The advice was given during a financial literacy and sensitisation seminar organised by NDIC officials at the NYSC orientation camp in Awka South Local Government Area of the state. The corporation urged the corps members to embrace what it described as a smart financial lifestyle built around earning, saving, investing and spending wisely. The Communications Manager of NDIC, Chinenye Chimezie-Amadi, advised the corps members to exercise caution when choosing where to save their money, stressing the importance of using deposit-taking institutions insured by the corporation. She urged them to develop the habit of budgeting, distinguishing between their needs and wants, and setting aside part of their earnings for emergencies and future investments. According to her, many people earn money without keeping track of how they spend it, making it difficult for them to build savings. “Our presence at the orientation camp is to help you learn a kind of life you need to live in future as you begin to make decisions for yourselves. “Some people won’t have savings, but you see them carrying expensive hairs and mobile phones. That is living a false life. We are looking at a situation where you save for emergency and for your future,” she said. Amadi urged the corps members not to dismiss the possibility of saving because of their present earnings, saying even small amounts could accumulate into substantial savings when set aside consistently. She also advised them to prioritise essential expenses before discretionary spending and develop the habit of paying themselves first by setting aside a portion of their income. On the choice of financial institutions, she warned against depositing money in unregulated schemes offering unusually high returns, urging them to verify that their banks were insured by NDIC. “Even when you have a house, you still need to set aside your house rent as a way of saving. If you do it consistently, you will be surprised at the amount you save,” she said. The NDIC Controller, Enugu Zonal Office, Mr Chidi Nwankwo, urged the corps members to acquire financial literacy skills ahead of their transition from national service into the labour market. Speaking on the topic, ‘Know Your Deposit Protection: A Practical Guide for NYSC Corps Members’, Nwankwo explained the corporation’s role in protecting depositors and outlined the applicable deposit insurance limits. He advised the corps members to confirm that any deposit-taking bank with which they intended to transact was insured by NDIC, explaining that eligible deposits were protected within the limits prescribed for different categories of financial institutions. item.title: Nvidia: ‘I’d Be Honoured To Return,’ Jensen Huang On Possible Reinstatement
item.description: Former Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang has said he would be willing to return to the position if the company’s board of directors considers his reinstatement to be in its best interest. Huang made the announcement in a statement posted on his X account on Tuesday, his first public comments since stepping down on November 12, following revelations about alleged extramarital affairs and concerns over his personal conduct. The former chief executive said he had received an outpouring of support from Nvidia employees, investors, business partners and customers, with many urging him to return amid the company’s ongoing challenges. “Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” he wrote. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO.” Huang, however, acknowledged that his personal conduct had fallen short of the standards expected of the company’s leadership and expressed regret over the difficulties his actions had created for the board. “I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret,” he said. “I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation.” (FILES) Jensen Huang, co-founder and CEO of Nvidia Corp., speaks during a news conference in Taipei on May 21, 2025. US tech giant Nvidia said on July 14 it will resume sales of its H20 artificial intelligence chips to China, after exports were halted due to US licensing curbs. (Photo by I-Hwa Cheng / AFP) | I-Hwa Cheng / AFP His resignation followed reports of alleged extramarital relationships, including one involving an executive of Singapore-based cloud computing firm Megaspeed International, which is under US criminal investigation over allegations that it helped Chinese companies obtain advanced Nvidia artificial intelligence chips in violation of American export controls. The allegations have also drawn attention to Nvidia’s role in the global artificial intelligence industry and concerns over the possible diversion of advanced US technology to China. The controversy has weighed on Nvidia’s shares, adding to uncertainty surrounding the company, which until recently was the world’s most valuable publicly traded company. Huang’s possible return has attracted support from prominent figures in the technology industry, including billionaire entrepreneur Elon Musk and other artificial intelligence investors. An online petition calling for his reinstatement has reportedly attracted more than 190,000 signatures. US President Donald Trump also expressed support for Huang’s return on Monday. item.title: Presidential Election: We Were Blindsided In Lagos In 2023 – Fashola
item.description: Former Lagos State Governor and former Minister of Works, Babatunde Raji Fashola, has said the All Progressives Congress (APC) was caught off guard by its defeat in Lagos during the 2023 presidential election. That outcome is one he says the party is “working tooth and nail” to avoid in 2027. Speaking in an interview on Politics Today, Fashola said the APC never anticipated losing Lagos, the political base of President Bola Tinubu, to the Labour Party candidate Peter Obi. “We were blindsided in Lagos,” Fashola said on Tuesday during an interview on Politics Today. FILE PHOTO: Former Minister of Works, Babatunde Fashola. The former governor, however, argued that the result reflected the growing maturity of Nigeria’s democracy rather than a collapse of the APC’s influence in Lagos. According to him, electoral victories and defeats are part of democratic competition, and political loyalties can shift over time depending on prevailing circumstances. Drawing a football analogy, Fashola said political parties, like football clubs, do not win every match and must constantly adapt to changing realities. “In an election, sometimes you can’t win everywhere. Most times, you can’t win everywhere,” he said. Fashola explained that in previous elections, the APC had strategically redirected its efforts to regions that were becoming more receptive to the party. He suggested that a similar approach would be adopted as the ruling party prepares for the next general election. “It remains to be seen whether, as happened in 2023, Lagos flipped, whether Lagos will flip back,” he said. “And we’re working tooth and nail to ensure that we take back what we lost.” Although he said the party was blindsided in the 2023 presidential election, Fashola dismissed suggestions that Tinubu had been politically “demystified” by the defeat, insisting that opponents underestimate the President at their own risk. He maintained that the APC remains focused on convincing voters that the reforms being implemented by the Tinubu administration deserve continuity beyond 2027. The former governor, who argued that President Tinubu deserves a second term, dismissed the ideas and plans being shared by opposition candidates. “What are the other parties offering that is different, that is better, that is compelling as a reason to interrupt the process of reform, growth, and restructuring that is already underway?” he asked. He also queried what he described as the opposition’s alternative message, asking, “What is the alternative message to what we are currently dealing with? What is the compelling message? Obi contested the 2023 presidential election, finishing third nationally behind APC candidate Tinubu and Atiku Abubakar under the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). However, he defeated Tinubu in Lagos State, where he secured 582,454 votes against the APC candidate’s 572,606. The APC has ruled the metropolitan state for 27 years. item.title: ‘Even A Tomato Seller Knows Strait Of Hormuz’, Fashola Blames Global Conflicts For Economic Pressures
item.description: Former Lagos State Governor Babatunde Fashola has defended the economic policies of President Bola Tinubu’s administration, arguing that global developments, including the COVID-19 pandemic, the Russia-Ukraine war and conflicts in the Middle East, have contributed to the cost-of-living challenges Nigerians are grappling with. Fashola, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria, said Nigeria was not insulated from global economic pressures, particularly disruptions to supply chains, energy supplies and food markets. Speaking during an appearance on Politics Today, the former Minister of Works said the global economy was still recovering from the effects of the pandemic, which disrupted economic activity and production worldwide. He explained that shortages of goods following the pandemic had pushed up prices, while the Russia-Ukraine war further affected the supply of major energy and food commodities, including diesel and wheat. This aerial photograph shows boats anchored off Oman’s northern Musandam Peninsula near the Strait of Hormuz on June 27, 2026. (Photo by – / AFP Fashola also identified the ongoing conflict in the Middle East as another factor affecting global markets, particularly energy supplies and shipping costs. “It’s also important to contextualise the factors and the circumstances that have exacerbated the cost-of-living challenges,” he said. “Even the tomato seller knows the Strait of Hormuz and prices his or her goods according to replacement costs now.” ‘Helping Families In Need’ Fashola, a former Minister of Works, also backed President Tinubu for a second term, defending the administration’s response to challenges. Defending the Tinubu administration’s response to economic pressures, Fashola listed the minimum wage review, the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), tax reforms, and the introduction of compressed natural gas (CNG) as part of measures intended to ease the burden on Nigerians. He said the minimum wage review was one of the government’s early responses to the rising cost of living, aimed at putting more money in workers’ hands. President Bola Tinubu during the inauguration of the APC PCC. However, he argued that increasing wages alone could not address the problem, warning that continuously injecting cash into the economy could create what he described as “hyper-demand inflation”. Fashola said the government had also sought to address some of the major expenses that reduce household disposable income, including rent, transportation, healthcare and children’s education. He identified NELFUND as one of the interventions aimed at easing financial pressure on families by supporting students’ education. “Your disposable income goes to rent, goes to transport, and goes to health care, and goes to your children’s education. And NELFUND was, okay, we will help families in need,” he said. item.title: Atiku’s fuel subsidy reversal plan not realistic — Fashola
item.description: Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has challenged Atiku Abubakar to explain how he intends to fund his proposed return of fuel subsidy if elected president in 2027, describing the plan as unrealistic. Fashola said the former vice-president had not addressed the practical difficulties that could undermine the proposal, particularly Nigeria’s inability to fully meet its crude oil production targets and persistent security problems in oil-producing areas. He made the remarks on Tuesday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today . The former Minister of Works and Housing questioned the source of the crude oil needed to supply local refineries and support a subsidy arrangement, given the country’s production challenges. “If we have refineries working, what is our current oil quota? Are we optimising it yet? No, because they are legacy issues, challenges with security people, vandalism. So where is this magic crude oil going to come from? People are entitled to ask,” he said. Fashola insisted that Atiku must demonstrate that the proposal can work rather than rely on promises to win public support. “If he can explain, good, let the people choose. But without proof, it is like abracadabra,” he said. He maintained that his criticism was directed at the policy and not the former vice-president personally. “The proposal is not realistic. I am looking at the proposal, not the personality,” he said. Fashola also questioned the consistency of Atiku’s position, noting that the former vice-president had supported subsidy removal during the 2023 presidential campaign. He said the change in position raised questions about the basis for the proposed reversal and what measures would make the policy sustainable. Fashola further argued that bringing back subsidy would involve legislative processes, as lawmakers would have to amend the existing legal framework to accommodate the policy. He wondered whether members of the National Assembly would be willing to support such a move, given its potential implications for public finances. The former governor also drew on his experience in the Buhari administration, saying subsidy payments had previously constrained the funds available to state governments. “I was in a government that was paying subsidy, and the states were not getting money. So are we going to go back to partial, near-zero returns, states borrowing money to pay salaries? Is that where you want us to go?” he asked. Atiku announced in August 2026 that he would restore fuel subsidy if elected president in 2027. He proposed a temporary, audited arrangement focused on petroleum products refined locally, arguing that it would help bring down fuel and transportation costs and ease the burden on households. Tinubu announced the removal of fuel subsidy during his inauguration on May 29, 2023, as part of his administration’s economic reforms. item.title: ‘Nothing Suggests To Me Tinubu Is Not Fit,’ Fashola Dismisses Health Concerns
item.description: Former Lagos State Governor Babatunde Fashola has dismissed concerns about President Bola Tinubu’s physical and mental fitness for office, saying he has seen nothing to suggest that the president is incapable of performing his duties. Fashola, a former Minister of Works and Housing, made the remarks on Tuesday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today , where he was asked whether he considered Tinubu physically fit to lead the country. “Nothing suggests to me that he’s not fit for it. Yes, he’s older. That doesn’t mean his mental capacity is gone. He’s still giving directives. And when I see him, he’s working. He’s still reading, authorising, minuting on things,” he said. President Bola Tinubu during his address to Nigerians for the 66th Independence Day anniversary on October 1, 2026. Questions about Tinubu’s health and physical condition have featured in public discussions since the 2023 presidential election campaign. During the campaign, concerns were raised by critics over his physical appearance, movements and stamina at public events. The debate continued after he assumed office in May 2023, with opposition figures and other critics occasionally questioning his capacity to discharge the responsibilities of the presidency. The concerns resurfaced in 2026 amid renewed scrutiny of his public appearances, including videos circulated online showing him moving cautiously at some events. The Presidency and the All Progressives Congress (APC) have repeatedly defended the president, maintaining that he is capable of carrying out his constitutional responsibilities. Tinubu has also dismissed speculation about his health. In September 2026, following an extended stay in Europe, he told reporters that he was ready to “work, walk and kick.” ‘More Mature’ The former governor, who worked closely with Tinubu during his eight-year administration in Lagos from 2007 to 2015, said the president had become more experienced over the years. Asked to compare the Tinubu he knew in the early 2000s with the president he knows today, Fashola said the president had become more mature. “Well, a much more mature one, certainly, without doubt. I am not the chief of staff he employed in 2002. That’s 39 years. I was 39 then. I’m 63 now. So we must give him that credit for the experience he has gained,” he said. ﻿ Fashola acknowledged that Tinubu might no longer maintain the same work routine he had in the past, particularly when it came to keeping late nights, but maintained that the president remained capable of handling demanding responsibilities. “Maybe not keeping late nights that he used to do. item.title: Military aircraft crashes, 19 dead
item.description: A military transport plane crashed on Tuesday in the Siberian region of Kemerovo, killing all 19 onboard, Russian media reported, citing a statement from Moscow’s defence ministry. “An An-12 military transport aircraft crashed in the Kemerovo Region while on a scheduled flight. The plane went down in an uninhabited area. There were 19 people on board, including the crew, they all perished,” the Russian defence ministry was quoted as saying by state news agency TASS. The preliminary cause of the crash is a technical malfunction, TASS added. “A commission from the Russian Aerospace Forces is working at the site to establish all the circumstances of the incident,” the ministry’s statement was quoted as saying by RIA Novosti. Kemerovo region’s governor, Ilya Seredyuk, said earlier on Telegram that there had been an “aviation incident” near the village of Yagunovo. He added that “an aircraft, which was in transit through our region, has presumably crashed”. Seredyuk posted a video from the site in which multiple fire engines and ambulances could be seen, their lights blaring in the dark. item.title: Benue Justice Commissioner resigns with immediate effect
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice of Benue State, Prof. Timothy Ornguga, has resigned his appointment with immediate effect, barely one year and two months in office. The Attorney-General announced his decision in a resignation letter dated November 13, 2026, addressed to Governor Hyacinth Alia through the Secretary to the State Government, SSG. The letter, titled, “Resignation from the Appointment as Honourable Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Benue State,” formally communicated his decision to step down from the position with immediate effect. He disclosed that he had served the state for one year, two months and two weeks, expressing appreciation to Governor Alia for the confidence reposed in him and the opportunity to serve. The resignation letter, which bears an official receipt stamp dated November 16, 2026, stated: “I write with profound respect and deep sense of responsibility to formally tender my resignation from my appointment as the Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice of Benue State. The resignation is with immediate effect. Having had the privilege of serving in this esteemed capacity for the past one year, two months, and two weeks.” He further stated: “I consider it an honour to have been entrusted with the responsibility of serving our dear state and contributing in my own capacity to the administration of justice, the promotion of the rule of law and the advancement of good governance. I am sincerely grateful to Your Excellency for the confidence reposed in me and for the opportunity to serve.” Contacted, the Media of the former Justice Commissioner, Jude Ekpendu confirmed the development. Meanwhile, efforts to ascertain the circumstances surrounding his resignation were unsuccessful as the Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Chief Solomon Iorpev, said he was unaware of the development when contacted. item.title: FGN bonds undersubscribed by 9% in November auction
item.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan The Federal Government of Nigeria (FGN) bond auction in November 2026 was undersubscribed by 9.5 percent , attracting a total subscription of N1.81 trillion against N2 trillion offered by the Debt Management Office, DMO. This reflects decline in investors’ demand for the Federal Government of Nigeria (FGN) debt instrument. According to the November FGN Bond Auction result released by DMO , investors bid N1.81 trillion for bonds worth N2 trillion with total allotments rising by 25 percent to N1.5 trillion in November, down from N1.2 trillion allotted in October 2026. Four instruments were offered during the auction consisting 21 percent FGN March 2028 , 19.3 percent FGN April 2029, 17.94 percent FGN August 2030 and 19.89 percent FGN May 2033, with an offer of N700 billion, N250 billion, N750 billion and N300 billion respectively. Investor interest was strongest for the May 2033 bond, which attracted N766.4 billion in bids from 233 successful applicants. The bulk of allotments also went to this bond, totaling N676.6 billion. The March 2028 bond received N162.99 billion and a non competitive allotment of N50 billion while the April 2029 bond received N241.03 billion and a non competitive allotment of N30 billion. The August 2030 bond received an allotment of N336.12 billion. Clearing yields for the bonds were as follows: March 2028: 16.89 percent, while that of other bonds were 16.99 percent. The results reflect continuous declining appetite among investors for Nigerian government debt, even as allotments tightened compared with previous months. item.title: ‘The Proposal Is Not Realistic,’ Fashola Faults Atiku’s Fuel Subsidy Reversal Plan
item.description: Former Minister of Works and Housing, Babatunde Fashola, has faulted the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar’s proposal to restore fuel subsidy if elected president in 2027, describing it as unrealistic and questioning the availability of crude oil to sustain the policy. Fashola said the proposal lacked sufficient explanation on how the country would secure the crude oil required to support domestic refineries and maintain a subsidy regime. The former Lagos State governor spoke on Tuesday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today , where he argued that Nigeria’s existing challenges with crude oil production, pipeline vandalism and insecurity raised questions about the feasibility of Atiku’s proposal. “If we have refineries working, what is our current oil quota? Are we optimising it yet? No, because they are legacy issues, challenges with security people, vandalism. So where is this magic crude oil going to come from? People are entitled to ask,” he said. Fashola added that Atiku needed to explain how he intended to implement the proposal, insisting that Nigerians should be allowed to assess its feasibility before deciding whether to support it. “If he can explain, good, let the people choose. But without proof, it is like abracadabra. Because the reality that will come then is that he will say that, ‘I didn’t know that there was not enough crude oil.’ That was what happened,” he added. ﻿ When asked whether his position was that Atiku’s proposal was feasible, Fashola replied: “The proposal is not realistic. I am looking at the proposal, not the personality. “In this environment, it is very easy to throw promises at people. When the rubber hits the road, reality sets in. First question is, in 2023, didn’t he see through this when he was making the promise to remove the subsidy? And that goes to a question of credibility. Those who believe at face value that promise, he will come back and tell you that, ‘Oh, I changed my mind. I didn’t think through it,’” he said. Fashola argued that restoring the subsidy would require more than a presidential declaration, noting that legislative backing would also be necessary. “Subsidy is not just about, ‘I said it.’ It will come down to the real economy, and legislators will have to repeal a law to say subsidy is now lawful. How many legislators are ready to stake their election on going back to subsidy? Those are the real issues,” he said. According to him, all the major presidential candidates in the 2023 election had promised to remove the subsidy, and Atiku needed to explain what had changed to justify his current position. “Is it because people are impacted? It’s true. But what are you going to do differently? Where are you going to find the money to sustain what you are offering? It’s not sustainable,” he said. item.title: 2027: Weigh alternatives before rejecting Tinubu’s reforms – Fashola tells Nigerians
item.description: …Says cost-of-living crisis is global …Subsidy return will hurt federation revenue …Defends Lagos-Calabar highway By Juliet Umeh Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has urged Nigerians to weigh opposition parties’ proposals before rejecting President Bola Tinubu’s reforms, saying the country should not “abort this journey mid-term” without considering the alternatives. Fashola, a former Minister of Works, spoke on Channels Television, where he said voters should be helped to make informed choices ahead of the 2027 general election. “What are the other parties offering that is different, that is better, that is compelling as a reason to interrupt the process of reform and restructuring that is already underway?” he asked. He acknowledged the hardship many Nigerians face but said the cost-of-living crisis was not unique to Nigeria. “Anybody who is right-thinking will concede that the cost-of-living challenge is now a global challenge,” he said, citing the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic and conflicts that disrupted energy and food supplies. Fashola said: The government had introduced measures including a higher minimum wage, support for students through the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, NELFUND, and tax reforms.” He said the policies were aimed at easing pressure on households, while acknowledging that there was “a distance between policies, programmes, projects and results.” On the removal of petrol subsidy, he said a return to the policy would have consequences for government revenue and the funds available to states and local governments. “Subsidy is not just about ‘I said it, I did not say it’. It has to be paid for somewhere. One of the things that suffered because of that was the monthly receipts into the federation account.” Fashola challenged politicians proposing a return to subsidy to explain how they would fund it and what they would do differently. “I want to see rigour, I want to see detail, I want to see numbers,” he said, adding that Nigeria also needed to explain where the crude oil for subsidised supply would come from, given constraints on production. Fashola said the government deserved credit for maintaining the subsidy removal, despite the hardship it had caused. “What this government deserves commendation for is not falling over on the sword and saying because the people like it, let’s bring it back,” he said. He cited the introduction of compressed natural gas, or CNG, as one of the measures aimed at reducing living costs. Defending the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, Fashola said it had reduced travel time to the Lekki Port. “It took me 40 minutes from Ikoyi to get to that port. Traditionally, when I went to visit that site when I was governor, it used to take me all of one and a half hours. A 90-minute journey is now 40 minutes. “Go and calculate the fuel savings in that corridor, and the relief to people’s disposable income,” he said. Fashola also pointed to jobs created by construction activity along the route

item.title: Tiger Woods to return to competitive golf next month
item.description: Tiger Woods will return to competitive golf for the first time in more than two years next month when he tees off at the Hero World Challenge event in the Bahamas, organisers said on Tuesday. Woods, 50, was named in the line-up for the limited field PGA Tour event taking place in Albany from December 3-6. It will mark the first time Woods has played an official PGA Tour event since July 2024. The 15-time major champion has battled injuries and legal problems since his last appearance. In March he was involved in a rollover car crash in Florida which led to him having his driver’s license suspended for five years. Authorities determined the 15-time major champion had not been drinking alcohol but found he appeared to be impaired. Woods, who has undergone multiple back operations and surgeries on severe leg injuries suffered in a separate 2021 California car crash, had two pills containing the opioid painkiller hydrocodone in his pocket. He refused a urine analysis and was charged, jailed and released on bond. Woods initially pleaded not guilty to charges of DUI (driving under the influence) with property damage and refusing to submit to a lawful test. Days later, he said he was “stepping away” to seek treatment and focus on his health. Since the crash, Woods has travelled outside the United States to seek treatment at an inpatient facility, reportedly in Switzerland. He made his first public appearance since his arrest at the PGA Tour’s Travelers Championship in June, and later struck a plea agreement which led to his driver’s license being suspended. Woods has not won a tournament since a victory at the ZoZo Championship in Japan in 2019. The post Tiger Woods to return to competitive golf next month appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: INEC warns against attacks on staff, threatens sanctions
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has warned against any form of harassment, intimidation or physical attack on its leadership, staff members or ad hoc workers by political supporters. INEC ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‍‌‌‌⁠‍⁠‌​Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, gave the warning on Tuesday in Abuja at the 2026 Goodluck Jonathan Foundation (GJF) Peace and Security Conference. Amupitan, represented by INEC National Commissioner, Mrs May Agbamuche-Mbu, described election officials as public servants discharging a sacred constitutional duty. He warned that assaulting or threatening them constitutes a direct assault on the Nigerian state and would be met with decisive legal consequences. Amupiatan also condemned the widespread incidents of political violence, intimidation and attacks on campaign convoys and party supporters recorded in some parts of the country in recent weeks. According to him, democracy can not flourish in an atmosphere of fear and bloodshed. “Let me issue a clear and unambiguous warning to all political actors, sponsors and their foot soldiers: “The law will take its full course and security agencies working alongside the commission will go after the promoters and perpetrators of violent campaigns without fear or favour. “Equally, I must sound a stern warning against any form of harassment, intimidation or physical attack directed at the leadership, staff or ad hoc workers of INEC by supporters of any political party—whether within Nigeria or abroad. “Election officials are public servants discharging a sacred constitutional duty; assaulting or threatening them is an assault on the Nigerian state and will be met with decisive legal consequences,’’ he said. Amupitan reminded political parties and candidates of the provisions of the Electoral Act 2026, noting that sections 96 and 97 prohibit abusive language, private thugs and use of force to intimidate voters. He said that the Act raised financial penalties five-fold, imposing fines of up to five million Naira or 12 months imprisonment on individuals and up to 10 million Naira on political parties for initial breaches. The INEC chairman added that under Section 148, INEC was statutorily empowered to prosecute electoral offenders directly upon receiving case files from the police. On physical security and logistics, Amupitan said that the commission was leveraging the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES) to secure the electoral terrain against insurgency, banditry and communal tensions. To tackle digital misinformation on elections, he said that INEC had established a dedicated Artificial Intelligence Division within its ICT Department. He said that the department was established to monitor database anomalies, verify digital assets and counter deepfakes, synthetic broadcasts and Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference (FIMI). item.title: Abia records 60% drop in maternal mortality — Govt
item.description: …Renovates 190 PHCs, functionalises 123, Polytechnic rector emerges Administrator of the Year By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Abia State Government has announced a 60 per cent reduction in maternal mortality between 2024 and 2026, claiming that the state now has the second-lowest maternal mortality rate in the country. The government attributed the improvement to ongoing reforms in the health sector, including the rehabilitation of primary healthcare facilities and increased investment in healthcare delivery. Commissioner for Information, Prince Okey Kanu, disclosed this during a briefing on the outcome of this week’s State Executive Council meeting at Government House, Umuahia. He was represented by the Special Adviser to the Governor on Media and Publicity, Mr Ferdinand Ekeoma. Kanu said the administration had made significant progress in its efforts to revitalise primary healthcare, disclosing that 190 of the 200 primary healthcare centres earmarked for renovation under Project Ekwueme had been completed. Of the renovated facilities, 123 had been functionalised to provide essential medical services, while 27 had been equipped with solar power, with work progressing on nine additional centres. He also announced the completion of all 77 World Bank-supported health projects in the state. In another development, the Commissioner disclosed that the Aba Campus of the College of Nursing Sciences had secured an increase in its admission quota from 75 to 120 students following an accreditation exercise by the National Nursing and Midwifery Council. The new quota, according to him, was communicated in an accreditation report released on November 13 and reflected growing confidence in the state’s investment in nursing education and healthcare manpower development. Meanwhile, the Rector of Ogbonnaya Onu Polytechnic, Aba, Dr Christopher Okoro, has emerged Administrator of the Year in a nationwide poll organised by Leadership Excellence Award. Kanu said Okoro secured 148,267 votes in the exercise, which recognised his contributions to institutional transformation, human capital development and technical and professional education. He attributed the recognition to developments recorded at the institution under the Rector, including a student population increase of more than 6,000, improved infrastructure and better staff welfare. The Commissioner also said the state government remained committed to education development, noting that the sector continued to receive 20 per cent of the state’s annual budget. On public health surveillance, the government reported that Abia recorded no cases of Ebola, Lassa fever, COVID-19, diphtheria, cholera, mpox or yellow fever during the period under review. item.title: Kano woman allegedly hires men to kill co-wife’s children for inheritance
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Kano State Police Command has arrested a 20-year-old woman and three others over an alleged plot to kill her husband’s four children from another wife to enable her only son to inherit his father’s properties. The suspects were arrested following the abduction and killing of a 14-year-old boy, identified as Mahmoud Auwal, who was allegedly targeted as part of the plan. The Police Public Relations Officer, CSP Abdullahi Haruna Kiyawa, disclosed this on Tuesday. According to the police, the victim’s mother reported his abduction on April 29, 2026, at Danbare Quarters in Kumbotso Local Government Area of Kano State. Following the report, the Commissioner of Police, Ibrahim Adamu Bakori, directed operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Squad to investigate the incident. The command said its operatives arrested the first suspect, Muhammad Musa Isma’il, 20, of Sharada Quarters, Kano, on November 3, 2026. “During interrogation, he confessed to luring the victim on April 20, 2026, and identified Abubakar Muhammad Isah, 27, and Auwal Muhammad, 26, as his accomplices,” Kiyawa said. The police said the suspects allegedly conspired to kill the teenager and abandoned his body at the scene. His remains were later recovered by police officers attached to Kwalli Division while on patrol and taken to the mortuary of Sir Muhammad Sunusi Specialist Hospital. Further investigations led to the arrest of Hajiya Rukayya Auwal, 20, of Mararaba Quarters, New Karu Local Government Area of Nasarawa State, whom the police identified as the alleged mastermind. The command said the suspects claimed that they carried out the crime on her instructions. It added that investigations revealed that Rukayya was the deceased’s father’s other wife and allegedly wanted to eliminate all four children of her co-wife so that her only son would inherit their father’s properties. “The principal suspect also allegedly engaged another group of thugs to attack Muhammad Musa Isma’il in Mararaba, Karu Local Government Area of Nasarawa State, in a bid to stop him from revealing the crime,” the police said. The command said the suspects would be charged to court after the conclusion of investigations. The Commissioner of Police condemned the killing and assured the victim’s family and members of the public that the command would ensure justice was served. He also called on residents to continue providing credible information to the police to assist in preventing and detecting crime. item.title: Two die, Gombe APC chairman, campaign DG injured in crash
item.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The Gombe State Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Mohammed Dantata Ndus, and the Director-General of the party’s 2027 Governorship Campaign Council, Sa’du Hassan, have sustained injuries in a road accident that claimed two lives in Dasan Yunusa community. The accident occurred on Tuesday along the Deba-Talasse Junction while the two party officials were travelling to join the campaign entourage of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya in Balanga North Local Government Area of the state. The APC State Campaign Council confirmed the incident in a statement, identifying the deceased as Haruna and Kabiru, both indigenes of Dasan Yunusa. It said the two APC chieftains sustained injuries and were receiving medical attention at the Federal Teaching Hospital, Gombe. Preliminary accounts indicated that the accident occurred when the driver conveying the party officials reportedly swerved to avoid a head-on collision with a motorcycle carrying three persons, which allegedly appeared suddenly at the junction. The vehicle reportedly veered off the road in the process, resulting in the fatal incident. Confirming the accident, the Gombe State Sector Commander of the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), Samson Kaura, said he had received information about the incident but was awaiting comprehensive details. Kaura confirmed that the APC chairman and the campaign council’s Director-General were receiving treatment, adding that further information would be provided as investigations progressed. The campaign council expressed sorrow over the incident and extended its condolences to the bereaved families, the people of Dasan Yunusa and others affected by the tragedy. Meanwhile, Governor Yahaya, who was leading the APC campaign activities in the area, visited Dasan Yunusa following news of the accident to commiserate with the bereaved families and community leaders. The governor described the incident as painful and unfortunate, noting that the loss of two lives had cast a shadow over what was intended to be a day of political engagement with the people. He urged the bereaved families and residents to accept the tragedy as the will of Almighty Allah. Yahaya prayed for the repose of the souls of the deceased in Aljannatul Firdaus and for strength for their families to bear the loss. As part of efforts to support those affected, the governor donated N5 million to the families of the deceased and the community leadership. He also prayed for the speedy recovery of those injured, particularly Ndus and Hassan, who were reported to be stable and responding to medical care. The governor’s visit and donation followed the fatal accident that disrupted the party’s campaign activities in the area. item.title: New Nasarawa police chief warns against extortion
item.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia The new Commissioner of Police in Nasarawa State, Sheikh Mohammed Danko, has warned officers and personnel against intimidation, extortion, unlawful detention and abuse of police authority. Danko, who has assumed duty as the 32nd commissioner of police in the state, said the police uniform represented a responsibility to serve the public and not a licence to operate above the law. He replaces Muhammed Shettima Jauro, who has been elevated to the rank of Assistant Inspector-General of Police. Addressing journalists at the command headquarters in Lafia, Danko said his administration would not tolerate corruption, excessive use of force, harassment or any misuse of police authority. He said: “Any officer found engaging in misconduct, political partisanship, corruption, or abuse of power will face immediate and appropriate disciplinary and legal actions.” The commissioner said complaints against police personnel would be treated seriously and thoroughly reviewed through the appropriate channels. He added that officers found culpable would be held accountable, irrespective of their positions, while personnel who discharged their duties honourably would receive the command’s support. Danko also cautioned political actors against using their offices or influence to intimidate citizens, provoke violence, obstruct lawful police duties or shield individuals from accountability. He directed officers to remain professional and non-partisan, warning against political pressure and private interests that could compromise their responsibilities. On security, the commissioner warned criminal elements involved in kidnapping, armed robbery, drug trafficking, cult-related activities and other violent crimes that the command would respond through intelligence-led and lawful operations. He also warned individuals providing shelter, weapons, information or other support to criminal networks that they could face the full weight of the law. Danko called for greater cooperation between the police and residents, urging community leaders, traditional institutions, youth groups and business owners to report suspicious activities through appropriate channels. He said public cooperation was essential to effective policing and reaffirmed the command’s commitment to protecting residents, enforcing the law impartially and strengthening public confidence across the state. The commissioner also advised residents against taking the law into their own hands or confronting suspects, warning that such actions could endanger lives and jeopardise investigations. item.title: Ebonyi demolishes shop over planning violations
item.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The Ebonyi State Government has demolished a shop on Ejiofor Street, Abakaliki, over alleged failure to obtain building plan approval and encroachment on designated land. The demolition was carried out by the Ministry of Capital City and Urban Planning. Speaking during the exercise, the Commissioner for Capital City and Urban Planning, Richard Ugo Idike, said the property owner commenced construction without obtaining the required building plan approval from the ministry. Idike explained that building plan approval was mandatory to enable the ministry assess proposed structures, conduct necessary inspections and provide professional guidance to ensure compliance with physical planning standards. He said securing approval before commencing construction would also allow the ministry to identify potential structural, environmental and planning concerns and advise property owners accordingly. The commissioner cautioned property owners and developers against unauthorised construction and encroachment on designated lands, warning that the state government would enforce relevant planning regulations against defaulters. Idike was accompanied during the exercise by the Head of the Town Planning Department, TPL Esther Nwite, other town planners and members of the ministry’s task force. He urged residents, developers and property owners in Abakaliki to obtain the necessary building plan approval from the ministry before embarking on construction projects. The commissioner reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to enforcing physical planning regulations and promoting orderly development in the state capital. item.title: Army Arrests Seven Suspects, Recovers 38 Phones, Mercedes-Benz In Plateau
item.description: Troops of Sector 1, Joint Task Force, Operation Enduring Peace, have arrested seven suspected criminals and recovered 38 mobile phones, a Mercedes-Benz E350, a motorcycle and other items in separate operations in Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State. The spokesperson for the Joint Task Force, Captain Chinonso Oteh, disclosed this while presenting the suspects at the task force headquarters in Jos, where he gave details of the operations. According to the task force, the arrests followed intelligence-led operations conducted on November 6 and 10, 2026, as part of efforts to curb armed robbery, phone snatching and other criminal activities in the state. In the first operation, troops acted on a report of a phone-snatching incident involving a gunman. The report led to the identification of the location of the stolen phone at Prime House Hotel, along Ring Road, Jos North. A raid on the hotel resulted in the arrest of five suspects. Items recovered during the operation included 26 mobile phones, 27 phone pouches, three MP3 devices, two earpods, an HP laptop, a dagger, four power banks and a Mercedes-Benz E350 with registration number Plateau BBK-01NB. The task force said a further search of the suspects’ vehicle, after it was towed to the Sector 1 headquarters, led to the recovery of 12 additional mobile phones, bringing the total number of phones recovered in the operation to 38. In a separate operation on November 10, troops deployed at Naraguta, working with members of the Vigilante Group of Nigeria, arrested two more suspects during a routine patrol. The suspects were reportedly found with a suspected stolen Boxer motorcycle and a toy pistol. The task force said the seven suspects and the recovered items would be handed over to the Plateau State Police Command for further investigation and possible prosecution. The Commander of Operation Enduring Peace, Major General Maxwell Dangana, reaffirmed the task force’s commitment to combating crime and sustaining peace across its joint operations area. He said the task force would continue to rely on intelligence-driven operations and collaboration with other security agencies and local vigilante groups to tackle criminal activities. Dangana also urged residents to remain vigilant and provide credible and timely information to security agencies to support efforts to restore and sustain lasting peace in Plateau State.
